products.title: 11SV625-MX Antique Venetian Opaline Seed Beads, 11/0 — Spring Garden Mix 10 Grams
products.body_html:
Genuine Venetian 11/0 seed beads from old Società Veneziana Conterie warehouse stock, in a three-color blend we're designating as Spring Garden Mix. This is a deliberate tricolor combination of soft butter cream yellow, gentle rose pink, and pale celadon green in roughly equal proportion. All three colors share a consistent opaline-luster finish — a soft, pearlescent sheen with gentle translucency — which gives the mix a unified, cohesive character despite containing three distinct hues. These beads were found bagged together with older SVC stock, and the consistency of the finish across all three colors indicates this was an intentional production colorway rather than a random accumulation of separate batches.

The palette is pastel, warm, and delicate. None of the three colors dominates — the butter cream, rose, and celadon sit at similar levels of saturation and lightness, creating a balanced, harmonious blend that reads as a single coordinated colorway rather than a mix of competing colors. The opaline-luster finish adds a gentle shimmer across all three, catching light consistently and tying the mix together visually. The overall impression is of faded wildflowers or a vintage spring garden — soft, feminine, and understated.

Each of the three color populations shows the minor internal variation typical of handmade Murano production. Some rose beads lean slightly warmer or cooler, some celadon beads carry more or less green, and the butter cream ranges from pale ivory to a slightly more saturated yellow. This bead-to-bead variation within each color, combined with the three-way color mix itself, produces a complex and visually rich texture when strung or stitched — no two sections of finished beadwork will look identical.

For beadwork and design, this mix offers a ready-made pastel palette in a single purchase. The balanced proportion and unified finish mean it can be used as-is for work where a soft, multi-tonal pastel effect is desired, or the three colors can be separated by hand for individual use. The opaline-luster finish on each color is consistent enough to work alongside the others or independently without a visible mismatch in surface character.

This colorway was recovered in a quantity of approximately half a kilogram from older SVC warehouse stock. Once this inventory is sold, we do not expect to source this specific mix again. Browse our full SVC specialty, opaline, and luster inventory for additional colorways and finishes.

products.title: Antique Venetian Micro Seed Bead Transparent Red Violet #1 - 10 Grams
products.body_html:
Antique SVC Venetian Transparent Micro Seed Beads — Red Violet #1

Genuine Venetian micro seed beads from old Società Veneziana Conterie warehouse stock, in Transparent Red Violet #1. This bead reads as near-black in massed quantity — a dense, dark field that gives little hint of its true color at casual viewing distance. But the transparent glass reveals its identity where light penetrates the thinnest parts of the bead — at edges, around perforations, and on individual beads that separate from the mass. The color beneath the darkness is a deep, rich red-violet — a dark garnet or wine-purple tone that emerges as warm, saturated flashes from within the seemingly black exterior.

This behavior is characteristic of deeply saturated transparent glass, where the color is so concentrated that the glass approaches opacity at normal bead wall thickness but retains its transparency at thinner points. The bead is not opaque and not simply dark — it is fully transparent glass that is saturated to the point of near-opacity, and the distinction matters. In finished beadwork, these beads will interact with light in ways that a true opaque black or dark purple cannot — catching and transmitting color at angles where light enters the glass, producing subtle, hidden warmth within what appears to be a dark field.

The surface has a soft, slightly metallic-looking sheen — a gentle reflectivity on the rounded bead surfaces that catches light almost like hematite. This is not a high gloss and not a flat matte, but a subtle luster that adds a quiet surface dimension to the bead's already complex optical character.

Sizing note for all SVC micro seed beads: These beads are sold as micro seed beads in the 16/0–24/0 range. Random sampling and measurement across our SVC micro inventory has confirmed that individual beads within any given lot range from approximately 0.9mm to 1.5mm, spanning multiple nominal size designations. This is characteristic of hand-drawn Murano micro production, where the extremely fine cane diameter made precise size control difficult at this scale. The variation is inherent to the manufacturing process, not a sorting or grading inconsistency on our part. We disclose this range rather than assigning a single size that does not accurately represent the lot.

Color consistency across the lot is excellent. Minor debris may be present, consistent with warehouse stock handling.

For restoration and traditional beadwork, deeply saturated transparent beads like this one were used where the maker wanted darkness with hidden life — areas of a design that read as nearly black under normal conditions but reward close inspection or angled light with unexpected warmth and color. This is a different material from an opaque black, a flat dark purple, or a lighter transparent violet — each behaves differently in finished work, and matching the correct depth, color, and transparency is essential for accurate restoration. products.title: 12SV146-28 Antique Venetian 12/0 Seed Bead Opaque Red #28 - 10 Grams

Genuine Venetian 12/0 opaque seed beads from old Società Veneziana Conterie warehouse stock, in Red #28. The surface finish is flat matte — dry and non-reflective, absorbing light rather than bouncing it. This is among the most matte finishes we've cataloged across any color, and it contributes significantly to the bead's dark, subdued character. The matte surface makes the color read as slightly darker than it would under a gloss finish, and removes any surface sparkle or shine that might lighten the visual impression. The result is a bead with a quiet, dense presence — it sits heavily in a design without calling attention to itself through brightness or reflectivity.

There is subtle variation across the lot. Some beads lean slightly warmer or carry a touch more brightness, while others are darker and more fully muted. This range is natural to hand-drawn Murano production and is minor — the lot reads as a cohesive single colorway rather than a mix. Bead profiles are a mix of rounded and slightly barrel-shaped forms, with the shape variation typical of 12/0 handmade seed beads. Proportionally large perforations are visible throughout.

For restoration and traditional beadwork, dark, muted reds like this one served critical roles as grounding and outlining colors — deep red accents that provided weight and seriousness alongside brighter primaries. The specific combination of the oxblood tone and the matte finish means this bead reads very differently from a glossy cherry or a bright opaque red, even at a distance. products.title: 12SV276-2M Antique Venetian 12/0 Seed Bead Transparent Frosted Blue #1 - 10 Grams
products.body_html:
Antique SVC Venetian Frosted Transparent Seed Beads, 12/0 — Blue #1

Genuine Venetian 12/0 seed beads from old Società Veneziana Conterie warehouse stock, in Frosted Transparent Blue #1. This bead introduces a sixth finish category to our SVC inventory — frosted transparent, where transparent glass has been given a matte, sandblasted-style surface treatment that diffuses the glass's natural clarity while preserving its underlying color depth.

The result is a bead with a unique dual character. The surface reads as soft, velvety, and matte — chalky and dry, absorbing light rather than reflecting it. But beneath that frosted exterior, the transparent glass retains its full color saturation and depth. Where the frosting is thinner — particularly around the perforations and on beads with less uniform surface treatment — the underlying transparent blue breaks through as bright, saturated flashes of color. The effect is a bead that appears muted and soft from one angle and reveals hidden intensity from another, like looking at deep blue through a layer of frost or fog.

The color is a medium-deep blue with a noticeable violet lean — more purple-shifted than a pure cobalt, approaching ultramarine or blue-violet territory. This violet quality is characteristic of the glass formula, not the frosting, and is visible both on the matte surface and where the transparent glass shows through. The overall impression is a rich, complex blue with more warmth and purple depth than a straight cobalt.

Shape variation across the lot is noticeable, with a mix of barrel-shaped and more rounded profiles. This is consistent with hand-drawn Murano cane production. Color consistency is good, with the bead-to-bead variation being primarily in the degree of frosting rather than the underlying glass color.

For restoration and traditional beadwork, frosted transparent beads occupy a very specific niche. They were used where the maker wanted the color depth of transparent glass without the sparkle and gloss — a muted, soft-surfaced bead that still carried more internal color than opaque glass could achieve. Substituting a standard transparent, an opaque, or a greasy bead will not replicate the frosted transparent's specific combination of matte surface and deep internal color. The finish type must match the original. Browse our full SVC blue, transparent, and specialty finish inventory to compare against your reference material.

The surface finish has a soft, slightly chalky satin quality rather than a high gloss — this may be characteristic of the original glass formula or the result of long-term storage, but either way it gives the bead a matte, aged appearance that distinguishes it from the shinier finish typical of modern Czech or Japanese seed beads in similar colors.

Color consistency across this lot is excellent. There is very little bead-to-bead variation, suggesting a stable, well-mixed glass batch. Sizing is uniform for hand-drawn Murano production, with the minor shape irregularities typical of the process.

For restoration work, this particular shade of blue is worth noting. Greasy blue and light blue beads were among the most historically significant colors in the Venetian trade bead palette, and period originals that have aged and softened over time frequently present in exactly this muted, dusty range rather than the brighter blues a modern buyer might expect. Blue #35 occupies a useful position for matching original beadwork where the blues have faded or mellowed — it reads as period-correct without the need to artificially age a brighter bead. For projects calling for a more saturated cornflower or medium blue, see our other blue colorway listings.

Genuine Venetian 8/0 white heart seed beads from old Società Veneziana Conterie warehouse stock, classified as Burnt Orange per the original SVC sample book. A note on color: viewed on its own, this bead presents as a bright, confident red and could easily be mistaken for a cherry colorway. The burnt orange classification becomes clear in context — placed alongside the deeper, cooler cherry and crimson white hearts in the SVC color range, this bead's warmer undertone separates it. It sits on the warm side of the red spectrum, leaning toward orange without fully arriving there. The distinction is subtle but meaningful for color-matching purposes.

This is a useful nuance for buyers to understand. Antique Venetian color classifications were established relative to the full production palette, not in isolation. A bead that reads as red to the modern eye was designated burnt orange because, within the SVC range, it occupied the warm end of the red family — distinct from the cooler, deeper reds that carried cherry or crimson designations. We've verified this classification against the original sample book and are listing it accordingly, while noting that product photos accurately represent the bead as it appears in hand.

The outer glass layer is translucent with a glossy finish, and the white core beneath brightens the color in the way characteristic of quality white heart construction. Color consistency across the lot is excellent, with minimal variation — this appears to be a clean, single-run batch. Sizing is uniform for hand-drawn Murano production.

At 8/0, this is a versatile working size for both restoration and new traditional beadwork. The warm red tone is particularly relevant for matching original beadwork where the reds have shifted toward orange over time through light exposure and aging, or for pieces where the original maker was working with this same warm-red end of the white heart spectrum. products.title: Antique Venetian Light Rose with Dark Cranberry White Heart 6/0 - 20 Grams
products.body_html:
Antique SVC Venetian White Heart Seed Beads, 6/0 — Light Rose with Dark Cranberry

Genuine Venetian 6/0 white heart seed beads from old Società Veneziana Conterie warehouse stock. This lot is defined by a striking two-tone character: a warm, lighter rose-red and a deeper, cooler dark cranberry coexist in roughly equal proportion throughout the batch. Unlike lots where one color dominates and the other appears as an occasional outlier, here the two tones are balanced partners — distinct enough to read as separate colors side by side, but clearly products of the same production run rather than a post-production mix.

The lighter rose beads lean warm, with an orange undertone that lets the white core show through prominently, giving them a bright, open quality. The darker cranberry beads sit at the opposite end — a cooler, wine-leaning red with more density in the outer glass layer, where the white core recedes and the color deepens toward burgundy. Between these two poles, individual beads land at various points along the spectrum, creating a naturally variegated effect when strung or stitched together.

This kind of two-tone variation within a single batch speaks to the realities of hand-drawn Murano production. The red outer glass was applied over the white core cane before drawing, and differences in the thickness and thermal history of that outer layer produced meaningfully different color outcomes across the same run. The result is a bead lot with built-in visual complexity that no single-color modern production can replicate.

Surface finish across the lot is consistently glossy, and the 6/0 sizing is relatively uniform for handmade production. White cores are intact and cleanly formed throughout.

For restoration and traditional beadwork, the dual-tone character of this lot is particularly practical. Rather than needing to source warm reds and cool cranberries separately and blend them by hand, this batch provides a natural, period-correct mix of both. Strung as-is, it produces the kind of organic color variation that's characteristic of original 19th and early 20th-century beadwork, where the maker was working from exactly this kind of variegated old stock.

products.title: Antique Venetian Faded Plum Red White Heart 11/0 - 10 Grams
products.body_html:
Antique Venetian 11/0 "Gold Ruby" White Hearts — Early SVC Production (c. 1898–1900), Faded Plum Red Variant

For collectors and restoration artists who understand the significance of what they're looking at: we've acquired a small quantity of uncirculated 11/0 Cornaline d'Aleppo white hearts from old Società Veneziana Conterie warehouse stock. This particular lot displays a softer, plum-toned crimson — a natural variation in gold chloride coloring that results from subtle differences in batch chemistry, gold concentration in the outer glass layer, and the inherent unpredictability of working with colloidal gold at furnace scale.

The SVC consortium was founded in 1898 from the merger of sixteen Murano bead-making families, and this batch appears to date from its earliest years of production. Under filtered 365nm UV light, these beads show no fluorescence — consistent with gold-based rather than selenium or cadmium coloring, and supportive of a pre-1900s manufacture date. For context, selenium wasn't widely available as a glass colorant until around 1919, and the transition away from gold chloride was gradual, driven by cost and supply. Selenium-era reds are noticeably different in hue, tending toward a brighter, more orange-leaning red that lacks the depth and softness of gold ruby coloring. We encourage serious buyers to conduct their own independent testing and welcome questions about this lot. This plum variant is where the lot becomes especially interesting for restoration work. Anyone who has attempted historically accurate repair on 19th-century beaded regalia, bandolier bags, moccasins, or pipe bags knows the frustration of sourcing period-correct color matches. Original beadwork that has seen 120 or more years of light exposure, handling, and environmental aging rarely presents the saturated crimson of a fresh gold ruby bead. A deep red replacement, however chemically authentic, can read as jarring against the surrounding original work. This softer, plum-shifted variant bridges that gap — offering the correct underlying chemistry and surface character while sitting naturally alongside aged beadwork without announcing itself as new material.

These beads are uncirculated old stock, not recovered trade beads. They have not been through African or North American trade circuits, so there is no wear, no dirt accumulation in the perforations, and no stringing damage. The surface finish is intact. This is a small lot from finite warehouse stock, and we do not expect to source this colorway again.

products.title: Antique Venetian Dark Red White Heart 11/0 - 20 Grams
products.body_html:
Antique Venetian 11/0 "Gold Ruby" White Hearts — Early SVC Production (c. 1898–1900)

For collectors and restoration artists who understand the significance: we've acquired a small quantity of uncirculated 11/0 Cornaline d'Aleppo white hearts from old Società Veneziana Conterie warehouse stock. These beads display the deep, soft crimson characteristic of gold chloride coloring — the rich hue that predates the industry's gradual shift to selenium-based reds in the early twentieth century.

The SVC consortium was founded in 1898 from the merger of sixteen Murano bead-making families, and this batch appears to date from its earliest years of production. Under filtered 365nm UV light, these beads show no fluorescence — consistent with gold-based rather than selenium or cadmium coloring, and supportive of a pre-1900s manufacture date. We encourage serious buyers to conduct their own independent testing.

For those working on authentic 19th-century regalia restoration, this color match is exceptionally difficult to source. The later selenium-era reds shifted noticeably toward orange, making genuine gold ruby white hearts essential for historically accurate work. This is a small lot from finite old stock, and we don't expect to source this colorway again.

 Sold in 25g tubes.

The Beadsmith Bead Board makes creating custom jewelry easier than ever! This spacious beading board allows you to create and repair multiple designs at one time, or create matching pieces. It features various channels and layouts, including V-shaped, U-shaped, and straight channels, ideal for designing bracelets and making necklaces, especially multi-strand jewelry. The tray includes multiple recessed compartments, perfect for holding beads, findings, and components, with some versions even featuring a dedicated space for a needle. The flocked surface helps prevent beads from rolling around and keeps designs in place during the planning process.

Made in China
